item.title: Bloomington braces for CFP championship crowds and celebrations
item.description: Bloomington is preparing for a large influx of fans to celebrate the Indiana Hoosiers' College Football Playoff National Championship game against the Miami Hurricanes, with increased police presence, extended shifts, and added staff and security at local businesses. Students have the holiday without classes, and extreme low temperatures are expected outdoors.

item.title: ‘Excited’ Hoosiers head to Miami for battle in CFP National Championship
item.description: The Indiana Hoosiers are set to compete in the College Football Playoff National Championship for the first time. Indiana University alumni and fans are heading to Miami to support their team.

item.title: 43 animals rescued from ‘toxic’ living conditions; Evansville duo face 100+ charges
item.description: Joshua and Alee Nelson were arrested in Evansville on 106 animal neglect charges after police found 43 animals living in squalid conditions with no access to food or water.

item.title: ‘This is very real’: Gary mayor ready to welcome Chicago Bears to Indiana
item.description: The City of Gary, Indiana is making a serious effort to lure the Chicago Bears to the Hoosier State, identifying potential sites and releasing conceptual renderings of a new NFL stadium.

item.title: Cold weekend setup then a brief midweek thaw | Jan. 17, 2026
item.description: The 7-day forecast predicts a cold week with highs in the teens and twenties, wind chills in the single digits, and a small chance of snow showers, followed by a warm-up on Wednesday with highs near 40.

item.title: 5 Indiana cities make U.S. News & World Report’s top 250 places to live
item.description: Five Indiana communities, including Carmel and Fishers, ranked among the top 250 best places to live in the U.S. in 2025-2026, according to U.S. News & World Report's latest ranking.

item.title: Indianapolis bars brace for crowds of Hoosiers ahead of Monday’s IU game
item.description: Bars across Indianapolis are preparing for a busy Monday night as Hoosier fans plan to head out for IU watch parties, with many bars offering special deals and staffing up to accommodate the crowds.
